mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 0.5% signals a strong accommodative monetary policy, which typically leads to increased liquidity in the market and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative more than 40% of the time when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive more than 60% of the time when UNRATE rises by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) signals strong consumer demand, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative more than 40% of the time during periods of sustained RSAFS growth.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in a quarter signals a contraction in the supply side of the economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive more than 60% of the time when INDPRO declines by more than 2% in a quarter.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is above 7% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) decrease by more than 100,000 in a month, it signals a significant labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 7% and PAYEMS declines > 100k in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive more than 60% of the time when UNRATE > 7% and PAYEMS declines by more than 100,000.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% in a month, coupled with a decrease in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5%, signals a positive demand shock with controlled inflation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST rises > 10% and CPIAUCSL declines > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative more than 40% of the time when HOUST rises by more than 10% and CPIAUCSL declines by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3% YoY), a decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals a potential misalignment of monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive more than 60% of the time when CPIAUCSL > 3% YoY and FEDFUNDS decreases.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) is below its 12-month moving average and GDP (GDPC1) growth is negative, it signals a supply-side recession, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive more than 60% of the time when INDPRO is below its 12-month moving average and GDPC1 growth is negative.
